answer: Executing a permutation of records on a tape costs a logarithmic factor beyond a linear pass (about tp log t per line for the length-t transform). Across all lines that would cancel the power-of-log saving the page is after, so the permutations are kept as index relabellings inside identities the algorithm uses anyway. The target permutation Q is never executed because the Divasov identity QF_t u = conj(a) . (a * (conj(a) . u)) / T rewrites the relabelled transform as two chirp phase multiplications around one totipuv (the wiki's name for the wrapped product of sequences) of length T; the relabelling becomes part of a convolution that is performed anyway. The source permutation R is never executed because it commutes with pointwise products (a permutation of a pointwise product is the pointwise product of the permutations), and the same R appears on both forward transforms and in front of the opposite transform. The identity R F^+ R = F^+ holds because multiplying indices by a unit t and then by its inverse just relabels the summation index, so (R F^+)[(R F u) . (R F v)] = u*v / S^2 with no R left to execute. The convolution is therefore computed without any sort.

citations.quote: A sort on every line would undo the saving of a power of $\log n$, so the permutations stay inside the formula.
the permutations of Sikusup stay inside the transform identity, where one is absorbed by a convolution and the other cancels.
They are kept inside the identity, never executed: carrying them out would sort $t$ records of about $p$ bits on a tape, costing about $tp\log t$, which would cancel the power saving.
The identity converts the transform together with $Q$ into a totipuv, so $Q$ never has to be executed as a sort.
The factor $s_i$ in the chirp is what encodes $Q$.
An entrywise product pairs entries at the same position, so $\pi(a\cdot b)=(\pi a)\cdot(\pi b)$ for any permutation: scrambled forward outputs multiply to the scrambled product.
Each $t_i$ is a unit modulo $s_i$ and $R$ applies $R_{t_i}$ on axis $i$, so tensoring gives $RF_{\boldsymbol s}^+R=F_{\boldsymbol s}^+$.
Keeping that order costs nothing: a pointwise product does not care how positions are listed, provided both factors use the same order, and the opposite transform can be run to read that order.
Thus the retained source permutation cancels when computing a convolution, and no sort occurs across the whole chain.
Executing $Q$ means sorting data on tapes, which costs a logarithmic factor beyond a linear pass, the kind of factor the power saving removes.

key_idea.statement: The target permutation is folded into the phases of a chirp-weighted convolution, so relabelling the output of the transform costs nothing beyond a convolution the algorithm already performs.
key_idea.quote: The identity converts the transform together with $Q$ into a totipuv, so $Q$ never has to be executed as a sort.

stuck.quote: Conjugating input and output turns a routine for $RF_{\boldsymbol s}$ into one for $RF_{\boldsymbol s}^+$, since conjugation flips the exponent's sign and commutes with the real permutation $R$.
stuck.note: I followed that conjugation flips the sign of the exponent, but I could not see why the algorithm needs an opposite-transform routine at all, nor how conjugating input and output produces one. The step is stated, not shown.

stuck.quote: So both the forward and the opposite transform are available only in the form with $R$ in front.
stuck.note: I could not tell whether this is an established result of the construction or an assumed premise. The page does not say how the algorithm achieves this form.

stuck.quote: The middle transform has its output relabelled, which is a single use with nothing to cancel against.
stuck.note: The middle transform is not named on this page. I had to infer from the identity on the zom page that it is the length-t transform between the two resampling maps.

stuck.quote: The product of the chirp phases at $j$, $j-k$ and $k$ is the Fourier kernel evaluated at the relabelled frequency, so the relabelling sits in the phases and costs nothing beyond a convolution the algorithm performs anyway.
stuck.note: I followed the words, but why the phases at j, j-k and k give the relabelled frequency is not shown on this page. I got past it only by going to the Divasov derivation, where the square is expanded.

stuck.note: This identity is asserted here without proof. I accepted it only after finding its substitution proof on the zom page, so for this page alone I was taking it on trust.

reason: Answered from five opened pages (zom, roz, pap, kur, fam; 5 of 15 opens). Both halves of the question are supported by quotes. Confidence is moderate to good: the source side depends on R F^+ R = F^+, which I followed through its substitution proof on zom. The target side depends on the Divasov expansion of the chirp square. The conjugation step that the wiki uses to get the opposite-transform form of the source identity is the least clear part, and I did not use it for the core argument.
